sources.title: Canada sharpens focus on study permit finances; proof of funds under scanner - The Economic Times
sources.ai_summary: Canada's Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has updated guidance for study permit applications, directing officers to scrutinize not just the amount but also the source, stability, and credibility of applicants' funds more broadly than before. An ApplyBoard analysis of 1,370 refusal letters found inadequate proof of finances was the leading rejection reason at 47%, while approval rates for major source countries including India (13 percentage points) and Nigeria (8 percentage points) improved during the first four months of 2026 despite the stricter requirements. Canadian educational institutions are being urged to shift from volume-based recruitment to focusing on applicants better prepared to meet the stricter financial documentation standards.

sources.title: Canadian immigration officials increase their scrutiny of study permit applicants’ financial documentation
sources.ai_summary: Canadian immigration officials are increasing scrutiny of study permit applicants' financial documentation, leading to a 43% drop in new applications but a 9 percentage point increase in the approval rate to 35% between January and April 2026. IRCC updated its guidance on July 24, 2026, directing officers to thoroughly investigate funding sources and request supplementary financial evidence for all cases rather than just high-risk environments. Analysis by BorderPass and ApplyBoard indicates that unclear proof of funds remains the primary reason for refusal, prompting recommendations for stricter documentation standards like six months of bank statements and sponsor job letters.
